purpose:

outstripped by projected demand, and two special schools, Oakleigh
Junior School and Mapledown Secondary School, will be
oversubscribed from September 2026 onwards. Due to the urgency of

meet the most urgent need for September 2026. This report requests

phase 1 of the project.

purpose:
At its
meeting on 5th February 2025, Cabinet approved Council
entry into a new contract with its Local Authority Controlled
Company (LACC); Barnet Education & Learning Service Limited
(BELS) for the provision of Education & Skills (and associated)
Services, commencing on 1st April 2025 for 5 years (with the
potential to extend for a further 3 years subject to satisfactory
performance and available budget).
Cabinet also approved the early termination of the existing
contract (to conclude on 1st April 2025), to enable the
implementation of a new agreement that establishes more
advantageous and contemporary terms. The parties are separate legal
bodies but the revised contract is
designed to better reflect the relationship between the parties,
underpinned by shared objectives and a strong commitment to
collaborative, partnership-based working.

Authority was delegated (by Cabinet) to the Chief
Executive in consultation with the Leader to finalise and
enter into and agree the terms of the
contract, scope of services to be based on paragraph 1.9
ofFuture deliveryof theBarnet Education
and Learning Service (BELS) (see ‘Background
Papers’ section 9.1 of this report).
This report outlines the areas
of material change to the contractual arrangement, notably the
transition from a predominantly commercial framework/arrangement to
one that more accurately reflects the Council’s relationship
with BELS. The revised agreement is grounded in a shared commitment
to delivering education services, with a strong emphasis on aligned
goals, partnership working, and a collaborative ethos between the
parties.  This report also confirms the budget and the
scope of services.

decision_maker: Executive Director Communities, Adults and Health
purpose:
Parks and open spaces
are a vital part of life in Barnet. They support health and
wellbeing, bring people together, and help protect the environment.
As our communities grow, so do the needs and pressures on these
spaces, encompassing population growth, climate change, the impact
on local wildlife and recreational
demands. 

 
To respond to these
changes and build on what has already been achieved, a new Parks
and Open Spaces Strategy (2026–2036) has been developed. The Strategy sets
out a clear vision and actions showing how we aim to care for and invest in
our green spaces over the next decade. It will help ensure that our
parks continue to meet the needs of residents, now and in the
future. 

 
The strategy has been
shaped by feedback from residents, community groups, and partners,
and reflects both local priorities and national best practice. It
is designed to be flexible and deliverable, with a focus on making
the most of what we have and working together to protect and
enhance Barnet’s green
spaces. 

 
Following approval at
Cabinet 18 November
2025 of the Draft Strategy
2025-2026, the Draft Strategy was subject to a public
consultation that ran from 19 to the 7
January 2026. A total of 142 representations
were received. As
the consultation is now complete and the
new Strategy can be approved
the Parks and Open
Spaces Strategy dates have been amended to run
from 2026-2036 which differs
to the dates noted in
the Draft
Strategy at Cabinet. 

 
Our vision for Barnet
over the next ten years is “to provide quality, inclusive and
sustainable parks and open spaces that enhance wellbeing, celebrate
local identity, enhance biodiversity and empower
communities”.

decision_maker: Executive Director Assurance and Public Protection
purpose:
The Cross Council Assurance Service (CCAS) is a
national framework enabling public sector
organisations—including local authorities, health bodies,
housing providers, and other eligible entities—to access
high-quality internal audit and advisory services. CCAS was
originally established in 2014 and led by the London Borough of
Islington, before ownership transferred to Barnet in April 2020.
The framework has grown significantly, with 66 organisations
(including 59 local authorities) drawing down services as of 30
September 2025.

The current framework, which commenced 1 April 2020
for a four-year term with two optional one-year extensions, is set
to end on 31 March 2026. The current framework is a single provider
framework and the suppliers appointed to this framework are PwC
(PricewaterhouseCoopers) for Internal Audit, Advisory and
Anti-Fraud (Lots 1, 2 and 4) and Mazars for Risk Management (Lot
3).

To ensure the Council can continue providing
effective internal audit and advisory services beyond 31 March
2026, Cabinet authorised on 5 February 2025 (through approval of
the Annual Procurement Forward Plan 2025/26), the procurement of a
new CCAS framework to commence by 1 April 2026. Barnet, in
consultation with the London Boroughs of Islington, Kensington
& Chelsea, Waltham Forest, and Southend-on-Sea City Council, is
leading this procurement exercise.

The new multi-supplier framework will be split into
two lots and the successful suppliers to be appointed to the
framework are:

Lot 1: Internal Audit – Forvis Mazars, KPMG
and PwC

Lot 2: Advisory Services – Forvis Mazars, KPMG
and PwC

The initial term is three years (to 31 March 2029),
with the option to extend for up to five further years (to 31 March
2034). The framework is designed to maximise flexibility,
cost-effectiveness, and innovation, and will be accessible to all
UK local authorities and a wide range of public sector
bodies.
This report seeks authorisation
for officers to enter into the new framework agreement, ensuring
Barnet and other public sector organisations can continue to
benefit from CCAS’s proven model of service delivery. The new
framework will support statutory requirements, corporate
priorities, and collaborative working, while promoting innovation
and best practice across the sector.

by Cabinet.

proceed with the disposal either via the use of The Barnet Group
estate agency ‘Bumblebee’ or at auction.

purpose:

approval to proceed with the final year of an optional 2-year (1+1
years) extension to the Security contract for services related to
physical guarding, reference 211018. The original term of the
contract was for a 3-year fixed term with the option to extend for
a further 2-year (1+1 years) term. The contract is inclusive of an
uplift to the London Living Wage (LLW) and CPI (Consumer Price
Index) in line with the current rates. 
 
The provider for this service
is Blue 9 Security Limited (“Blue 9
Security”).
 
The Tender for security
services was conducted and moderated in September 2021 with a
commencement date of 14th September
2021. Blue 9 Security
were awarded the Security contract for a total 5-year term with an
initial 3-year term with the option to extend for a further 2-years
(1+1 years) subject to performance review, value of contract and
budget.
 
The original annual cost for
Security Services was £1,314,015 per annum with a total spend
for the 5-year full term expected to be £6,570,075.
Compliance with the London Living Wage was detailed within the
contract from the outset. However, in order to meet the unforeseen
uplift in London Living Wage, it has been necessary to include
indexing to the Consumer Price Index (CPI), to be documented in the
form of a Deed of Variation to the initial contract.
 
The current expiry date for the
first year of the optional 2-year extension (1+1 years) is
13th September 2025. The second optional year (of the 2
available years) will lengthen the contract giving a new expiry
date of 13th September 2026.
 
In addition, other departments
have opted to use the services of the Security Contract on an
additional ad hoc basis. The annual value of the contract is
currently at £1,660,311. The new annual value including
compliance with the London Living Wage (LLW) and the Consumer Price
Index (CPI) is £1,661,204.
 
The increase of £892 has
been budgeted for within the Council Managed Estates Budget. The
full breakdown of service costs across the contract has been
detailed within section 5 of this report. The breakdown will
identify cost reductions in some areas due to service reductions
and increases in other areas due to LLW and CPI uplifts.

purpose:
This report concerns a request
by the Council’s joint venture partner Related Argent for
their plot development subsidiary RACAL IUK BXIP2 PLOT 14 Limited
(RA), to take partial possession of the building (Core C) and grant
under-leases within the Plot 14 development ahead of full Practical
Completion of the new building. As residents are given one
month’s notice prior to moving in, this will allow residents
to move prior to Christmas.
The Plot 14 head-lease dated 17
October 2022 between (1) London Borough of Barnet (2) RACAL IUK
BXIP2 PLOT 14 Limited and (3) the Related Companies L.P prohibits
the head tenant from granting under-leases until after full
Practical Completion (PC) is certified, without consent of the
Landlord (i.e. the Council as freeholder).
The building is not expected to
achieve full PC until 1st December 2025, but RA's
contract administrator (Cast) is in a position to confirm partial
possession of Core C now and to provide the Council with a
statement from Cast that it has determined, based on the
information provided to it, that Core C of the building is deemed
to have been practically completed. 
The head tenant is fully
responsible for the property and its condition, and the Council has
the benefit of usual tenant covenants to protect its position as
freeholder.
There is therefore very limited
risk to the Council in making this decision, for the reasons given
in this report, and so enabling the plot developer to grant
occupational under-leases to incoming residents.

purpose:
The Localism Act 2011(“the Act”)
introduced the Community Right to Bid (“CRTB”). Under
sections 87 and 93 of the Act the Council must maintain a list of
assets of community value in its area and a list of land nominated
by unsuccessful community nominations. 
A building or other land is of community value if having regard to
the Act and the Assets of Community Value (England) (Regulations
2012 in the Council’s opinion there is an actual current use
of the building or other land, which is not an ancillary use, which
furthers the social wellbeing or social interests of the local
community, and it is realistic to think that there can continue to
be non-ancillary use of the building or other land which will
further (whether or not in the same way) the social wellbeing or
social interests of the local community.
On 24 September 2025, an
application was received by the Council for the application for
Former Quinta Youth Club & Village Green, Mays Lane, EN5 2AP to
be listed as an Asset of Community Value (ACV)
